utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May we have the appearances beginning with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court. Dirk Ryneveld, Suzanne Hayden, Dan Saxon, and Andrew Powell is our case manager, here in our special capacity at the request of the Chamber to lead evidence in this Rule 77 proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Peter Haynes for Avramovic and Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. AVRAMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Avramovic, attorney from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NESKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Goran Neskovic representing Mr. Steven Todorovic, on behalf of Mr. Brashich.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Zecevic on behalf of Milan Simic on the merits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This morning the Chamber gives its decision in the contempt proceedings. The Trial Chamber, having considered all the evidence in the Rule 77 proceedings, now delivers its judgement on the allegations of contempt against the two respondents, Milan Simic, an accused before this Tribunal, and his formal lead counsel, Branislav Avramovic. On 7th July 1999, the Chamber issued a scheduling order calling upon Branislav Avramovic and Milan Simic to respond to allegations that each, by his respective acts as set forth in the scheduling order, committed a contempt of this Tribunal by knowingly and wilfully interfering with its administration of justice and by offering a bribe to and interfering with a potential witness with the intention that he should give false testimony before this Tribunal in favour of Milan Simic. As to the first respondent, Branislav Avramovic, the Chamber unanimously finds that the allegations of contempt have not been established beyond a reasonable doubt. As to the second respondent, Milan Simic, the Chamber unanimously finds that the allegations of contempt have not been sustained beyond a reasonable doubt. Accordingly, neither respondent is in contempt of this Tribunal. A written opinion stating the reasons for today's decision will follow shortly. That concludes the sitting of the Trial Chamber. The Court now stands adjourned.
